transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-20 09:32 PDT | Duration: ~55 minutes | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Sasha (Redwood CSM), Alex (Redwood SRE); Dr. Elena Martinez (Aurora VP Eng), Ravi Shah (Aurora SRE), Monica Gomez (Aurora InfoSec), Tom Briggs (Aurora Platform)

Summary: Quick follow-up to the 10/18 incident where inference latency spiked and evictions occurred in the Dedicated pool. Goal: review postmortem action items, confirm mitigations, align on next steps for benchmarks and patch schedule.

Topics: incident timeline, root-cause (autoscaler / OOM interplay), mitigation (cache tuning, pod density), reliability improvements (canaries, tracing), compliance handoff (SOC2, KMS), benchmark plan for Dedicated hosts.

09:32 Maya (Redwood AE): okay hi everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll try to keep this tight i know everyone's busy. big thanks for the notes you sent, elena, helped a lot.
09:33 Dr. Elena Martinez (Aurora): yeah thanks. want to start with a one line from oak from our side — production saw two big spikes of traffic and then the autoscaler didn't recover fast enough, we hit queueing and some requests timed out.
09:34 Jordan (Redwood SE): yeah the initial thing we saw in our traces was KV cache pressure plus a mis-sized autoscaler window, so the pool scaled but not quick enough, and then the padding we had for OOMs was insufficient, that combined. also some of the nodes ran on an older kernel which made memory reclaim behave slightly differently, so some of that bit-rotted.
09:35 Ravi (Aurora SRE): hmm uh we did notice a kernel upgrade window on that cluster the night before, not related to our rollout tho.
09:36 Maya: right. quick Q — is everyone comfortable with the timeline in the doc? jordan uploaded the spoj timeline? (laughs) i mean the incident timeline to the shared drive last night.
09:37 Monica (InfoSec): timeline looks fine, but we still need the exact list of logs to be archived for the audit, and confirmation on KMS key access.
09:38 Sasha (CSM): noted, we'll include the exact log retention policy and a link to the KMS access control matrix.
09:39 Jordan: just to add — the root cause chain we believe is: sudden traffic spike -> KV cache thrash -> memory pressure -> OOM killer evicting model processes -> autoscaler reacts but after SLO breach. Also there was an unrelated degraded disk on one node that increased GC pauses, which made the reaction slower.
09:41 Tom (Platform): when you say "KV cache thrash" do you mean prefix cache or the full kv cache? we've been tuning the prefix settings to reduce warmup.
09:42 Jordan: mostly prefix/prefix-KV interactions; warmup combined with longer sequences caused the per-request mem to spike. our suggestion is to set a smaller prefix cache TTL for that workload and enable per-route kv prefetching.
09:44 Dr. Elena: okay, so the immediate mitigation we asked for — what did you push? i saw a config change that reduced concurrent in-flight requests.
09:45 Maya: yes we lowered the max_concurrent_requests on the route for aurora-prod to limit queueing while we run the benchmark. that reduced tail latency but hurt throughput briefly which is expected.
09:46 Ravi: we also kicked an emergency restart of the affected nodes, that helped temporarily.
09:47 Jordan: for the medium-term fix we've got three PRs: one to change autoscaler sensitivity and cool-down, one to adjust the caching policy, and one to add a pre-warm step for larger sequence lengths. that pre-warm is kind of like a warm shard that primes the kv cache.
09:49 Monica: on encryption — can you confirm that logs we share are redacted and that KMS keys are customer-owned?
09:50 Sasha: yes logs we share will be redacted for PII, and we have a customer-managed KMS option for Dedicated/private deployments. i'll send the KMS integration doc.
09:51 Dr. Elena: thanks. also audit log retention — we need six months for this environment. can you confirm retention settings?
09:52 Maya: default is 90 days but for Aurora we can enable extended retention as an add-on, we'll send pricing and enablement steps.
09:53 Tom: one more ops question — you mentioned a canary deploy and automatic fallback. what's the rollback policy if the canary fails?
09:54 Jordan: our rollout plan includes a canary at 5% then 25% then 100% with automated health checks (latency, error rate). if the canary breaches thresholds we'll auto-fallback to previous model variant and route traffic to Hosted or Dedicated-compatible fallback. note sometimes the fallback path is transcribed as "Redwood Dedicate" in old notes but it's Redwood Dedicated, sorry for the noise.
09:56 Dr. Elena: that's fine, we just need the exact thresholds so our SREs can tune alerting.
09:57 Jordan: we'll share a table of thresholds and suggested alert rules.
09:58 Maya: ok onto benchmarks — aurora asked for a dedicated-host benchmark simulating your peak + 30% burst, correct?
09:59 Ravi: correct. also we want a run with your patched autoscaler and with quantized model variants.
10:00 Jordan: yep we'll spin up a dedicated bench cluster with the autoscaler fix and run both q4 and fp16 paths; expecting results in ~48 hours but depends on slots. we'll provide the test harness and replay script.
10:02 Dr. Elena: perfect. how about the timeline to patch? you said week of 10/26?
10:03 Maya: that's the target. jordan will cut the PR today and we'll schedule a canary for 10/27, full deploy 10/28 if canary is good.
10:04 Monica: for compliance handoff, we want the SOC2 artifacts and a short explainer of how audit logs are generated and stored.
10:05 Sasha: we'll prepare a document with screenshots and attach the SOC2 section, plus a short video walkthrough.
10:06 Ravi: i have one lingering ask — can you add additional tracing at the model inference level? right now traces show request time but not KV cache hit/miss per request.
10:07 Jordan: absolutely, we can add tags: kv_hit=true/false, seq_len, batch_size. that will help root cause later. it'll add a small overhead but plan is minimal.
10:08 Tom: any talk of costs? if we add tracing and extended logs, what's the billing impact?
10:09 Maya: tracing and extended retention are billed as add-ons; we'll send a cost breakdown in the follow-up.
10:10 Dr. Elena: ok to recap next steps?
10:11 Maya: sure — recap: (1) Redwood uploads full incident timeline and perf traces by 10/21, (2) Jordan runs KV cache repro and shares batch-config by 10/23, (3) Redwood shares SOC2/KMS docs and retention confirmation by 10/22, (4) Bench run of Dedicated hosts with autoscaler patch target week of 10/26, deliver results ~48-72h after run, (5) Patch canary 10/27, full rollout 10/28 pending health checks.
10:13 Dr. Elena: good. final note — please include the exact list of logs we'll receive for the audit so our compliance team can sign off.
10:14 Sasha: noted, will include.
10:15 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links and action items.
10:16 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: some product names transcribed oddly (eg "Redwood Dedicate"), occasional speaker label mismatches early on. references: incident timeline doc (link), SOC2 artifacts (link), bench harness repo (link) — links to be sent in follow-up.
